# libarchive / libarchive_fuzzer

OSS-Fuzz's fuzz target `libarchive_fuzzer` ([source](source/libarchive_fuzzer.cc), modified; see below) over libarchive (libarchive/libarchive at 3670ecf7).

Reads the input from memory (archive_read_open_memory) with all filters and formats plus raw and empty, the options zip:ignorecrc32, tar:read_concatenated_archives and tar:mac-ext, and the passphrase 'secret'. Per entry it calls 17 metadata accessors and reads the data a page at a time. It stops at ARCHIVE_EOF or ARCHIVE_FATAL from archive_read_next_header or ARCHIVE_FATAL from archive_read_data. Then it calls has_encrypted_entries, format_capabilities, file_count and seek_data on the archive and frees it. Nothing is compared. Each call first ignores SIGPIPE, as bsdtar and bsdcpio do.

## How this program differs from what OSS-Fuzz runs
- Linked against libarchive at commit 3670ecf7.
- In every build, getenv() returns NULL, getpid() returns 1 and mkstemp() uses a fixed name, so the program depends only on its input.
- A small driver reads the input file, calls the harness one to four times and prints each return value.
- The harness source is modified: source/libarchive_fuzzer.cc is OSS-Fuzz 955c6866's projects/libarchive/libarchive_fuzzer.cc with one Theorem Labs change. It ignores SIGPIPE at the start of each call, as libarchive's bsdtar and bsdcpio do, so a write to a filter program that stopped reading fails with EPIPE instead of killing the run.

## What the harness checks
The harness makes no check of its own beyond not crashing. Its halts statements say only that the code it calls never crashes, hangs or trips a sanitizer. Its agreement statements say only that the code never crashes or trips a sanitizer, and allow a run that never ends.

## Statements ([Statements.v](Statements.v))

**Blocked by the model.** On ordinary inputs each of these binaries uses non-blocking descriptors, queries or sets resource limits, installs signal handlers and starts threads, which this release's model treats as an error, so every statement here is false in this model for that reason alone. The program is not at fault; the statements become meaningful when the model covers it.
